newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Mirror in debt deal for Midland.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Mirror in debt deal for Midland.

text.p: British newspaper company Mirror Group Plc said on Friday it had arranged a five-year 600 million stg credit facility to refinance its debt and pay for its planned acquisition of Midland Independent Newspapers Plc.
Mirror executives also told reporters they expected initial cost savings of at least 5.0 million stg from its proposed 297 million stg acquisition of the regional newspaper group.
"That is an initial and very identifiable (estimate)," Mirror chief executive David Montgomery said during a telephone conference call.
He added that he did not expect the acquisition to run into problems with Britain's Department for Trade and Industry, which must clear the deal.

"There are plenty of precedents for the co-ownership of national and regional newspapers. So I can see no reason why we should not (receive regulatory clearance)" he said, adding that he did not expect a DTI decision before October.
The company expected the deal to be earnings enhancing in the first full year of ownership.
Montgomery said he could not say whether the acquisition would result in any job losses, noting that the company had yet to plan the integration with Midland.
He added that the initial cost savings estimate did not include job losses.
Under the deal, Mirror would offer 210p per share for Midland, with a partial share alternative.
The company said it would not issue more than 60 million shares as part of the deal, with the exact ratio depending on market conditions at the time of clearance.
Midland's shares rose 5.0p to 193.5, while Mirror's shares firmed 3.0p to 189 by 0835 GMT.

When asked how the deal would affect Mirror's market share, Montgomery noted that the company had about 54 percent penetration in western Scotland through its alliance with the Scottish Daily Record and Sunday Mail.
"We would imagine that we would at least replicate that sort of penetration in the Midlands with the addition of the (new) titles," he said.
He added that the deal was an extension of Mirror Group's strategy to cut costs by organising regional papers under a central infrastructure.
"This is an enterprise which we are very familiar with, and we know the businesses very well indeed, and the integration produces great efficiencies," he said.
Besides eliminating overhead costs, Mirror expected to reap benefits in production, distribution and purchasing from the Midland deal.
Midland forecast pre-tax profits of at least 13.2 million stg before exceptionals for the six months ended on June 29, a 59 percent rise versus the year-ago period.
"When you take that into consideration, and work out the price, I think you will see it's a very fair price," finance director John Allwood said.
